correctness.rationale: The stationary Lyapunov equation gives Sigma=(T/a)I. Gaussian finite-dimensional path reversibility is equivalent to symmetry of all lag covariance matrices. Rodrigues gives F_t-F_t^T=2e^(-at) sin(Ωt) PMP^T/Ω, and on any observation plane PMP^T=(ω·n)J. Sampling at Δ requires sin(kΩΔ)=0 for every integer k, equivalently the k=1 half-turn condition unless ω·n=0. Current j=Mx rho gives exactly 2Ω²/a. Two-block Gaussian covariance inversion yields K_t=4b_t²(1-det F_t)/det(I-F_tF_t^T), whose local expansion gives the pairwise slope; no full projected entropy-production rate is asserted. Independent 120 4x4 covariance/KL checks agree to 4.44e-16.

final_claim: For stationary 3D isotropic Ornstein–Uhlenbeck rotation with ω != 0, a two-plane observation is path reversible exactly when the plane contains ω; its samples at interval Δ are reversible exactly then or when ||ω||Δ is an integer multiple of π. The exact ordered-two-snapshot relative entropy has slope 2(ω·n)^2/a; full dissipation is 2||ω||²/a.
limitations: Equal restoring rates, isotropic three-component noise, 3D skew generator, orthogonal planar observation and even-parity reversal.
The observed reversible two-plane process need not be Markov and pairwise KL is not pathwise dissipation.
